findings.title: Open events beyond the first page are silently missed
findings.rationale: `Incident` requests only page 1 and treats its events as the complete result. `ListStatusPageEventsCLI` caps page size at 100 and returns pagination metadata, but the helper never follows it. The resolved-status guard and error handling do not prevent successful, incomplete lookups.
findings.why: Acceptance criterion ac-1 requires listing each open event. A successful first-page lookup does not establish that all events are resolved.
findings.suggestion: Follow the returned pagination metadata and inspect every page, preserving best-effort handling of lookup failures. Add a test with an open event on page 2.
findings.failureScenario: Resolve an incident with 101 status-page events, where the first 100 are resolved and the last is investigating. The lookup succeeds, but the helper prints no warning about the remaining open event.
findings.trigger: `incidents update --status=resolved` calls `statuspagewarn.Incident`, which always requests page 1 with `eventsPageSize`.
findings.verdictNote: 2 of 2 verifiers confirmed, 1 did not answer — internal/cmd/incidents/update.go:114 accepts --status=resolved and line 169 calls Incident after a successful update. internal/statuspagewarn/statuspagewarn.go:34 requests only page 1; internal/api/client.go:1850 caps its size at 100 and line 1907 returns pagination metadata. Incident ignores that metadata: if those 100 events are resolved, lines 40–46 return silently without inspecting an investigating event on page 2. The deliberate truncation comment at line 16 does not satisfy the warning about any remaining open events promised in README.md:170. Existing helper tests cover single-page results and lookup failures, not this pagination case.

findings.title: The suggested resolve command fails required-flag validation
findings.rationale: The warning prints `rootly status-pages events resolve <id>` as the command to run, but `eventsResolveCmd` marks `--message` as required. Cobra rejects the printed command before `runEventsResolve` executes. The existing validation prevents the public write but makes every printed remediation incomplete.
findings.why: The feature promises an actionable command for resolving the public entry; its suggested command cannot execute against the existing command contract.
findings.suggestion: Include a quoted `--message` placeholder in the printed command and explain that the operator should supply the public resolution message.
findings.failureScenario: Resolve an incident with an investigating status-page event, then copy and run the command from stderr. The CLI reports that the required `message` flag is missing and leaves the event open.
findings.trigger: Every open event emitted by `Incident` receives a command without the required `--message` flag.
findings.verdictNote: Producer: internal/cmd/incidents/update.go:169 invokes the warning after incident updates; internal/cmd/incidents/statuspagewarn_test.go:70 covers a resolved incident with an investigating event. internal/statuspagewarn/statuspagewarn.go:50 prints the resolve command without --message, which internal/cmd/statuspages/events_mutations.go:57 requires. Cobra validates required flags before RunE (/home/dev/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2/command.go:1007), so copying the printed command fails before resolving the event. Existing warning tests check command text, not executability. Intentional manual resolution does not explain the incomplete remediation.
